name: Rifampicin
route_note: Oral capsules on an empty stomach, alone or in fixed-dose TB combinations; IV formulation available.
targets: Bacterial DNA-dependent RNA polymerase beta subunit (rpoB)

discovery.by: Piero Sensi, Maria Teresa Timbal and colleagues (Lepetit)
discovery.note: A semi-synthetic derivative of rifamycin SV; the rifamycins were found in 1957 in Amycolatopsis rifamycinica (then Streptomyces mediterranei) from a soil sample near Saint-Raphaël, France.

tagline: Cornerstone of tuberculosis and leprosy treatment and a potent enzyme inducer
summary: Rifampicin is a semi-synthetic rifamycin developed by Lepetit in the 1960s. Its sterilising activity made six-month short-course tuberculosis treatment possible, and it is also central to leprosy treatment, staphylococcal biofilm infections and meningococcal prophylaxis. It is one of the most powerful inducers of drug-metabolising enzymes.
mechanism: Rifampicin binds the beta subunit of bacterial DNA-dependent RNA polymerase in a pocket next to the active site, physically blocking the elongating RNA after two or three nucleotides and so inhibiting transcription; it does not affect the mammalian enzyme.

Resistance in M. tuberculosis arises mostly from mutations in an 81-bp 'rifampicin resistance-determining region' of rpoB, detected by rapid molecular tests such as Xpert MTB/RIF. Rifampicin activates the nuclear receptor PXR, strongly inducing CYP3A4, other CYPs, UGTs and P-glycoprotein, which reduces levels of many drugs.
uses: Tuberculosis (first-line, with isoniazid, pyrazinamide and ethambutol)
Latent TB infection (alone for 4 months or with isoniazid)
Prosthetic joint and other staphylococcal biofilm infections (in combination)
Prophylaxis for close contacts of meningococcal and Haemophilus influenzae type b disease
Brucellosis and some nontuberculous mycobacterial infections

history.title: Rifamycins discovered
history.detail: Lepetit researchers isolate rifamycins from a soil actinomycete.

history.title: Rifampicin synthesised
history.detail: Lepetit chemists produce orally active rifampicin.

history.title: Leprosy MDT
history.detail: WHO recommends multidrug therapy for leprosy, including rifampicin, dapsone and clofazimine.

history.title: Xpert MTB/RIF
history.detail: WHO endorses the Xpert MTB/RIF test that detects TB and rpoB-mediated rifampicin resistance within hours.

history.title: Nitrosamine impurity
history.detail: The FDA reports 1-methyl-4-nitrosopiperazine (MNP) impurities in rifampin and allows temporary distribution above the usual limit to avoid shortages.

pk.metabolism: hepatic deacetylation to active 25-desacetylrifampicin; induces its own metabolism
pk.excretion: mainly biliary, with enterohepatic recirculation; partly renal

common: Orange-red discolouration of urine, sweat, tears and contact lenses
serious: Hepatotoxicity, especially with isoniazid and pyrazinamide
Clinically important interactions reducing levels of antiretrovirals, anticoagulants, hormonal contraceptives, azoles and immunosuppressants

facts: The name rifamycin was inspired by the 1955 French crime film 'Rififi'.
Rifampicin resistance is used as a marker for multidrug-resistant tuberculosis because it usually coexists with isoniazid resistance.
